common_name: North American Obscura-Group Fly (3rd-Chromosome Inversion & Two-Segment Sex Comb)

predecessor.note: Hawaiian picture-wing melanin-band rung. Not a stratigraphic ancestor; the assigned Drosophila chronoseries neighbour.

successor.note: Abdominal pigment rung associated with tan-locus evolution in the santomea literature. Not a stratigraphic descendant.

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila pseudoobscura (2.0 µm, detail scale)

governing_equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = largest real eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(D_u, D_v)
governing_equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
turing_conditions: (D_v f_u + D_u g_v)^2 > 4 D_u D_v det(J)
governing_equations.source: Turing 1952 Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37-72; the k_c minimizer of det(J - k^2 D) is the standard two-species formula used by Murray.

parameters.above_onset: D_v is 2 percent above the marginal value that places the determinant minimum on lambda = 1.961 um, so the fastest-growing mode remains on that rung
parameters.note: These coefficients are specific to the 2.0 um detail rung. They are not the alpha_scale / beta_offset power-law pair used by the 114 um pseudoobscura slot or by the planitibia and santomea primordium slots.

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) showed that a homogeneous steady state stable to reaction alone can be unstable to a finite band of wavenumbers when the inhibitor diffuses farther than the activator.

Richards et al. (2005) sequenced Drosophila pseudoobscura and documented chromosomal and cis-regulatory divergence, including the third-chromosome inversion system that defines this species. That paper does not measure a Turing wavelength.

Kopp (2011) reviews the sex comb as an evolutionary innovation. The common name of this slot records a two-segment sex comb; that structure sits at the tarsomere scale and is not identified with the 1.961 um mode.

The 1.961e-6 m figure is the assigned detail rung (tier 3_subcellular_um) of this chronoseries node. It is the wavelength the dispersion relation is tuned to select, not a published wet-lab period of an ocellar stripe in D. pseudoobscura.
